question.problem:
The equation of the parabola $y=7{x}^{2}-28x+18$ in vertex form is

$y=$
{{field-1}}$(x\,-$
{{field-2}}$)^{2}-$
{{field-3}}.
question.worked_solution:
To express the equation of the parabola in vertex form, we need to complete the square. 

First, we take out a factor of $7$ from the entire expression:

$$
\begin{aligned}7{x}^{2}-28x+18 & =7({x}^{2}-4x+\frac{18}{7})\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we complete the square for the expression inside the parentheses:

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}^{2}-4x+\frac{18}{7} & = \\ {x}^{2}-2\cdot 2\cdot x+\frac{18}{7} & = \\ {x}^{2}-2\cdot 2\cdot x+{2}^{2}-{2}^{2}+\frac{18}{7} & = \\ ({x}^{2}-2\cdot 2\cdot x+{2}^{2})-{2}^{2}+\frac{18}{7} & = \\ (x-2)^{2}-{2}^{2}+\frac{18}{7} & = \\ (x-2)^{2}-4+\frac{18}{7} & = \\ (x-2)^{2}-\frac{10}{7} & \end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we substitute this result back into our original expression:

$$
\begin{aligned}7({x}^{2}-4x+\frac{18}{7}) & = \\ 7((x-2)^{2}-\frac{10}{7}) & = \\ 7(x-2)^{2}-10\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, expressed in vertex form, the equation of the parabola is $y=7(x-2)^{2}-10.$
